note: The weak glottal makes 'do-(ʔ)â' land immediately as doʔâ (دعا, 'prayer'); 'saburam' (صبورم) and 'dide' (دیده) are clean words. But the middle 'dʒâ' floats free and the whole thing does not cohere into a Persian clause — a string of real words, not a sentence.
'sadâ' (صدا, voice) pops out. 'haride' is NOT Persian — the intended word would be xaride (خریده, 'bought') with x, not h; with h it is a non-word. Tail '-najam/-nayam' does not resolve to a word.
'hâli' (حالی) + 'bud' (بود, 'was') read fine and 'sar' (سر, 'head') is there, but the closing 'rumah/-rumah' is not a Persian word (rou-mâh would be forced). Fragmentary.

Best-parsing region. 'tanâhi' is one metathesis away from tanhâyi (تنهایی, 'loneliness'); 'budam' (بودم, 'I was') and 'alam' (الم, 'sorrow') are clean. 'tiram' hovers near tireh (تیره, 'dark') / tir (تیر) but doesn't settle. Reads almost like a broken line of verse.
'tâ' (تا, 'until') and 'budi' (بودی, 'you were') anchor the ends; 'did' (دید) and 'alam' sit in between but the medial 'da-lam' boundary is ambiguous. Words yes, clause no.

A row of disconnected real morphemes — ki (کی), tâ (تا), adam (آدم/عدم), rahim (رحیم) — with the weak glottal in 'tâ-(ʔ)a-dam' just marking a hiatus. No syntax binds them; reads as noise made of Persian-shaped beads.

gloss: … voice, you were not, on(to) the moon
note: Three genuine recoveries: 'sadâ' (صدا), 'nabud(i)' (نبود/نبودی, 'was/were not'), and 'mâh' (ماه, 'moon') with 'ru mâh' = روی ماه. The leading 'ro̞' and glue between them keep it from becoming a real sentence.

'mâh' (ماه) is solid; 'sude' is one sibilant off from shode (شده, 'became') — s for sh is exactly the foreign-tint you'd expect. 'râhim' splits between râh (راه, 'road') and the name Rahim (رحیم) and won't commit.

'tâ didan' (تا دیدن, 'until seeing') is the clear spine. 'kabut' is near kabud (کبود, 'livid/bruise-blue') or kabutar (کبوتر, 'pigeon'). The opening 'tanah' (a͡h weak) does NOT reach tanhâ (تنها) — the h closes the syllable instead of preceding â, so my ear gets tane (تنه, 'trunk/body') at most.

gloss: alone, alone, on the moon / on [her] face
note: Most Persian-sounding line. The reduplication pulls 'tanah tanah' toward tanhâ tanhâ (تنها تنها, 'alone, alone') and 'ru mâh' = روی ماه ('on the moon' or, idiomatically, a face). Still slightly off: the trailing weak -h in 'tanah' isn't the full tanhâ, so it's a strong impression rather than a certainty.
